greet: Ah, {name}, a listening ear at last! Sit, sit, and I shall give you a tale worth the price of your supper.
Well, well, {name}. Another soul in the firelight, and not a moment too soon.
Good evening, {name}. Mind the bench, it has a memory for the unwary.
Hark, {name}! The night is young and the ale is old, and both improve with company.
Greetings, {name}. The fire is warm and my throat is drier than a widow's wit.
Ah, {name}. You arrive as the third act begins, which is either fortune or a cruel jest of the gods.
Good eve, {name}! Shall I be your entertainment, or will you be mine? Both, I hope.
Oh, {name}, a face that does not turn away. You have made my whole evening, you have.
accept: Gladly! Lead on, and I shall spin the rest of the way as we go.
Oh, I am quite willing. Let us see what the evening grants us.
Yes, yes, I would be delighted. Do not keep me waiting, I beg you.
Aye, I am with you. A pleasant prospect after so long alone with my own voice.
Certainly. You have chosen wisely, and I shall tell you so twice before the night is out.
Done, then! I was hoping someone would ask before I had to ask myself.
Of course. Fortune favours the bold, and so, I suppose, do I.
Yes. Show me the way, and I shall fill the silence with something worth hearing.
Willingly. You have the courtesy of a patron, and I prize it above coin.
Yes indeed! Lead on, and mind you do not interrupt the good parts.
decline: No, thank you, {name}. My evening is spoken for by my own tongue.
I think not, {name}. Some offers are too small for a lady of my stature.
Alas, {name}, I must refuse. I have a grudge to nurse until morning.
No. You may ask again when you have something better to offer me.
Not tonight, {name}. I am in a sulk and sulks are very demanding companions.
I shall pass, {name}. Do not take it to heart; it is the wind speaking, not I.
Thank you, but no. The ballads have been calling me, and I must answer them.
No, {name}. I have set my heart on quiet, and I shall have it.
Regretfully not. You have a kind face, but I am already promised to the fire.
I decline, {name}. I am, as they say, out of humour and out of patience.
pressed: Excuse me a moment, I must attend to something that will not wait.
Forgive me, I shall return before you have finished frowning.
Hold my place, I am called away by a matter of some urgency.
I must step away briefly. Do not let the story die while I am gone.
Pardon me. Duty, of a most humble and inconvenient kind, calls me away.
Wait for me, I shall not be long. The night keeps its secrets for a while.
Excuse me, I am needed elsewhere for a short while, and I hate being needed.
Be patient, I return presently, with my dignity mostly intact.
Keep the seat warm; I must go and fetch what is owed to me.
content: I have said my say for now, and the rest may be saved for another night.
Enough for one evening. I shall leave you with the best of it unsaid.
That will do. Good company, but even a storyteller must rest her tongue.
I have had my fill of talk. Farewell for the present, {name}.
There, I have given you enough. Go and mull it over with your ale.
The tale is told as far as it goes tonight. I shall take my leave gracefully.
My voice is weary and my audience is, I trust, satisfied. Good night to you.
I have played my part for this hour. I withdraw to the wings.
Enough, enough. Even the finest tale grows stale when chewed too long.
I shall go now, {name}, before I say something I shall have to rehearse again.
closing: The bell has rung, and so must I. Good night, all of you, and sleep well.
Last call, is it? Then farewell to the fire and the ale and the faces.
Night falls and so does the curtain. Good night, friends, until the road calls again.
Closing time, and the tale must end with it. Good night to the lot of you.
The barkeep has spoken, and who am I to argue with a man holding a lamp? Good night.
All good things end at the bell, so I bid you good night and fair dreams.
Well, that is the last of the evening. Good night, and mind the stairs.
The fire is dying and so is my voice. Good night, one and all.
Time to take the road to bed. Good night, and keep your buttons close.
Farewell for tonight. May your dreams be kinder than my ballads were.
